summary: Thirteen standalone analysis/utility scripts sit around the training engine (self_organize.py) and read its logs, checkpoints and corpora. They fall into four groups: (1) log/record analysis — compare.py (paired bootstrap P(A>B) decision rule) and runs.py (a CSV registry of finished runs); (2) checkpoint readers — holdout.py (per-domain held-out probe out of a ckpt), prompt.py (generation, the deliverable), vocab.py (tokenizer cohort audit); (3) probes — probe_signature.py, probe_stability.py, probe_ckpt_geometry.py, keystone_probe.py, cl_bench.py; (4) corpus builders — fetch_big.py (HF streaming) and fetch_local.py (this machine's own Python source), plus sweep_domain_report.py which summarises sweep_domain_grid.sh. Only compare.py, sweep_domain_report.py, fetch_big.py, fetch_local.py, prompt.py and cl_bench.py have any automated caller; runs.py, vocab.py, holdout.py and all four probes are hand-run only. All thirteen parse; I executed compare.py, runs.py, vocab.py, prompt.py, holdout.py, cl_bench.py, keystone_probe.py, probe_stability.py, probe_ckpt_geometry.py, probe_signature.py, sweep_domain_report.py and fetch_local.py against a real checkpoint/log I generated. probe_signature.py is dead on its default settings (crashes in its own control arm); several report lines in compare.py, cl_bench.py and sweep_domain_report.py print verdicts that contradict the numbers printed beside them, or that no data can make fail. Every number produced by any of these is a signal about the configuration it ran under, not a fact about the architecture.

levers.name: --metric (compare.py)
levers.effect: selects held_out | d_order1 | train. Also selects the DIRECTION of every statistic via LOWER_IS_BETTER, and gates the cross-corpus warning.

levers.name: --gamma (compare.py)
levers.effect: Bouthillier meaningfulness threshold; splits 'significant' into meaningful vs not, and enters the Noether seed budget.

levers.name: --negligible (compare.py)
levers.effect: effect-size floor in b/B (default 0.03, the measured replication floor); below it the tool suppresses the seed-budget advice.

levers.name: MIN_PAIRS / NEGLIGIBLE / GAMMA / ALPHA / BETA / BOOT (compare.py)
levers.effect: module constants, not CLI-settable: 3 independent observations minimum, 0.03 b/B floor, 0.75, 0.05, 0.20, 10000 bootstrap draws.

levers.name: KNOBS (runs.py)
levers.effect: the 11 knobs recorded per row and compared against _SPEC in `stale`. Adding a knob here without it being on the EFFECTIVE line makes every parsed row read '<predates this knob>'.

levers.name: BYTES_PER_COHORT_CAP (vocab.py)
levers.effect: caps the corpus bytes read for --corpus. Named per-cohort but used as a whole-corpus cap.

levers.name: CKPT / DEVICE / GEN_LEN / GEN_TEMP / TOPK / REP_PENALTY / REP_WINDOW (prompt.py)
levers.effect: checkpoint path, device, generation length (default 200) and temperature (0.6), memory top-k, and the repetition penalty and its window. Settable as env or as KEY=VALUE on the command line.

levers.name: MEM (prompt.py)
levers.effect: 0/1. Enables the memory blend AND is the hidden precondition for GROUND — _recall returns [] when MEM=0.
levers.evidence: prompt.py:150, :98 `if SRC is None or not USE_MEM: return []`

levers.name: GROUND / GROUND_K / GROUND_CHARS (prompt.py)
levers.effect: retrieve source passages and silently prime the context with them. Inert unless MEM=1.

levers.name: DATA_MODE (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: 'synthetic' (default) uses order-2 Markov domains; 'real' loads data/train/<domain>/ and REPLACES N with the number of surviving corpora.

levers.name: MEM_CAP (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: store capacity. cl_bench main defaults it to 20000, cl_bench estimate to 300000, self_organize's registry to 200000 — three defaults for one name.

levers.name: LAMBDA (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: nominal memory blend weight in bpb(). Because the memory distribution always sums to exactly 1, LAMBDA is the WHOLE blend weight with no quality gating.

levers.name: REKEY (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: re-encode every stored key with the current model after each domain (the drift fix). Default 0, but both shipped callers set REKEY=1.

levers.name: WRITE_ADAPTIVE / WRITE_TARGET / WRITE_GATE (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: memory write gate. WRITE_ADAPTIVE defaults 0, which leaves memory.py's quantile gate dead inside the adaptive branch and the fixed WRITE_GATE threshold running — the same coupling self_organize.py prints a banner note about.
levers.evidence: cl_bench.py:29, :181-182; self_organize.py:5934-5936 "the quantile gate lives inside the adaptive branch, so WRITE_ADAPTIVE=0 leaves the fixed WRITE_GATE threshold running"

levers.name: CORRUPT_MODE (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: 'cross' (default) pairs a domain-1 context with another domain's token; 'shuffle' permutes within domain 1.

levers.name: ESTIMATE (cl_bench.py)
levers.effect: 1 = run the wall-clock projection instead of the benchmark.

levers.name: PROBE_SWEEP / PROBE_DRIFT_ON (probe_signature.py)
levers.effect: SWEEP=0 skips sections (a)-(g) and runs only the rekey-lag probe; DRIFT_ON appends the drift probe after the sweep. SWEEP=0 is currently the only setting under which the file completes.

levers.name: PROBE_STEPS / PROBE_POSMAX / PROBE_RUNS / PROBE_K_CENT / PROBE_MAXEVAL / PROBE_ENC_LR / PROBE_SEED / PROBE_STREAM_LEN / PROBE_JSON
levers.effect: encoder training checkpoints, ENC_POS_MAX multiples of WIN, run-smoothing widths, centroid pool size, eval cap per class, encoder LR, seed, stream length, optional JSON dump.

levers.name: PROBE_DRIFT / PROBE_DRIFT_BASE / PROBE_DRIFT_POSMAX / PROBE_DRIFT_R
levers.effect: lag ladder, encoder steps before the centroids are frozen, positive radius and run width for the rekey-lag probe.

levers.name: A= / B= / N= / NULLS= (probe_stability.py)
levers.effect: the two checkpoints, probe windows per corpus (512), and the number of size-preserving shuffles for the null floor (20).

levers.name: CKPT= / N= (probe_ckpt_geometry.py)
levers.effect: checkpoint (directory or .pt; prefers probe.pt) and probe windows per corpus (256).

levers.name: DOMAINS / DATA_DIR / DATA_MODE / STREAM_LEN / ENC_WARMUP / BENCH (all three probes)
levers.effect: set with os.environ.setdefault BEFORE importing self_organize, because self_organize builds its corpora at import time. BENCH=1 is inert here: it only gates main(), which the probes never call.
levers.evidence: probe_stability.py:31-37, probe_ckpt_geometry.py:24-30, probe_signature.py:39-43; self_organize.py:7807 `if bool(_i("BENCH", 0)):` inside main()

levers.name: GATE_COMP / GATE_V / GATE_REC / NP_TRUE (sweep_domain_report.py)
levers.effect: the pre-registered K3/K4 pass thresholds (0.80 completeness, 0.85 V, 0.85 boundary recall) and the true class count. NP_TRUE is a module global that parse() overwrites from whichever cell log it last saw.
couples_with: the order in which cell logs are parsed

levers.name: --dataset / --config / --field / --split / --data-dir (fetch_big.py)
levers.effect: which HF dataset, config, text field, split and in-repo subdirectory to stream. A preset resolves by short key OR by full dataset id.

levers.name: --shuffle-buffer / --seed (fetch_big.py)
levers.effect: streaming shuffle reservoir (default 10000) so self_organize's held-out TAIL is a sample rather than a block. Both are recorded in the manifest and a --resume with different values is refused.

levers.name: --min-score / --score-field (fetch_big.py)
levers.effect: drop documents below a dataset-native quality score; silently a no-op if the field is absent, so the file prints a NOTE when it skipped nothing.

levers.name: --resume / --shard-mb / --min-chars / --gb / --out / --domain / --token (fetch_big.py)
levers.effect: continue from the manifest, shard size in MB (512), minimum document length, target GB of text, output root, target domain directory, HF token.

levers.name: --domain / --out / --gb / --root / --ext / --min-bytes / --include-tests / --seed / --allow-short (fetch_local.py)
levers.effect: corpus name (also picks default extensions and search roots), output root, target GB, extra walk roots, extensions, minimum file size, whether to keep test trees, shuffle seed, and whether a short corpus is fatal.

levers.name: SHARD_MB / SEP (fetch_local.py)
levers.effect: shard size (256 MB) and document separator. The stated purpose is byte-compatibility with fetch_big.py so 'eng vs py' is not also 'downloaded vs local'.

bugs.title: prompt.py's memory blend is the exact ungated 50/50 mix that self_organize.py fixed — measured hp is identically 1.0
bugs.symptom: MEM=1 always takes exactly 50% of the probability mass from retrieval, however bad the nearest neighbour. `hp = dm.sum().clamp(max=1.0)` is meant to gate on match quality, but mem_dist scatters a softmax, so the sum is exactly 1.0 by construction. This is the same defect self_organize.py documents and fixed with MEM_GATE/MEM_CONF0/MEM_W ('hp was therefore identically 1.0 and this was an UNCONDITIONAL 50/50 mix at every position ... memory measured NET-NEGATIVE at every store size'). prompt.py is the tool the deliverable — generations — is read with, and it never got the fix.

Contrast self_organize.py:3260-3278 `_mem_w`, and its comment 'hp was dist.sum(), but read() scatters a SOFTMAX over the top-k, so dist ALWAYS sums to exactly 1.0 -- verified numerically.'

carry_forward.item: The memory blend weight `hp = dist.sum()` is ALWAYS exactly 1.0, because every reader scatters a softmax over the top-k. Any blend written as `(1 - lam*hp)*pm + lam*hp*pmem` is an unconditional lam-share mix with no quality gating. self_organize.py fixed this with `_mem_w` (MEM_GATE / MEM_CONF0 / MEM_W); prompt.py and cl_bench.py did not.
carry_forward.why: This single formula is the reason memory measured net-negative at every store size in the engine, and it is still live in both the tool that reads the deliverable and the tool that produces the continual-learning numbers. A rebuild must have ONE gated blend function that every caller imports.
carry_forward.evidence: self_organize.py:3260-3278 (`_mem_w` and its comment 'hp was therefore identically 1.0'); memory.py read(): `w = torch.softmax(tv / tau, dim=-1); dist.scatter_add_(1, toks, w)`; prompt.py:213-214; cl_bench.py:161-162; measured live: `SUM of memory distribution = 1.0`

carry_forward.item: A crossing is not a sample. On compare.py's unpaired branch, n_a x n_b crossings are NOT n_a*n_b independent observations — each run appears in n_other of them. Every threshold must count `min(len(A), len(B))` (or the shared-seed count when paired), never len(pairs).
carry_forward.why: This was already found and fixed once for the MIN_PAIRS guard and immediately re-committed four lines later in the seed-budget line. Any rebuild should compute the effective n ONCE and forbid len(pairs) downstream.
carry_forward.evidence: compare.py:256-267 and :289-292 (the fix) vs compare.py:339-343 (the same error surviving); reproduced: 'UNPAIRED (4x4 = 16 crossings, but only 4 independent observation(s) per arm)' followed by 'sample size is adequate (16 >= 5 needed)'

carry_forward.item: Direction is per-metric and must be applied to EVERY printed quantity, not just the statistics. compare.py orients the pairs for the bootstrap but leaves the per-seed diff column raw, so the headline and the table disagree in sign on d_order1.
carry_forward.why: The file's own header records that hardcoding lower-is-better once made every --metric d_order1 verdict name the wrong arm. The orientation is now half-applied, which is a subtler version of the same trap.
